B1.scope: Investigative journalism and open-source investigation practice: the hypothesis-based inquiry method (Story-Based Inquiry, UNESCO/Mark Lee Hunter), IRE and GIJN guides (following the money, public records, procurement and contracting investigations, document-driven reporting), Bellingcat/OSINT verification practice, newsroom investigation tracking (timelines, document logs, source maps), and community/citizen investigation guides. Include how journalists investigate delayed or over-budget public construction projects.

B2.scope: Legal and law-enforcement investigation practice: litigation case files and matter management, eDiscovery (EDRM model, document review, privilege, technology-assisted review), legal fact investigation (chronologies, cast of characters, issue outlines, e.g. CaseMap-style tools), police major-case management (MCM in Canada/UK: HOLMES, lines of enquiry, action allocation, policy file, the 'investigative mindset'; UK College of Policing APP on investigation), inspector-general and auditor investigation standards (CIGIE Quality Standards for Investigations, GAO Yellow Book, audit evidence).

B3.scope: Analysis and sensemaking: intelligence analysis tradecraft and structured analytic techniques (Heuer's Analysis of Competing Hypotheses, key assumptions check, indicators, the CIA Tradecraft Primer), the Pirolli-Card sensemaking loop (foraging and sensemaking), evidence grading (Admiralty/NATO source reliability and information credibility), argument mapping, and how investigators plan: lines of enquiry, collection plans, information requirements, objectives decomposition, re-planning as evidence arrives.

B4.scope: AI systems: agentic research and planning architectures (deep-research agents, plan-and-execute, ReAct, hierarchical task decomposition, re-planning, memory and scratchpads, long-horizon agents), document understanding (intelligent document processing, layout-aware parsing, schema discovery for unfamiliar documents, reading a long document by structure first: TOC, sections, then targeted extraction; purpose- or question-guided extraction; few-shot learning of a new document type and template induction), human-in-the-loop review and acceptance of AI-extracted facts, citation grounding and hallucination control, evaluation of such systems. Prefer primary sources (papers, official engineering docs, e.g. Anthropic, OpenAI, Google research posts, arXiv).

B5.scope: The procurement and public-works domain: the Open Contracting Data Standard (stages planning, tender, award, contract, implementation; parties, milestones, amendments, documents, the OCID) and its red-flags guides for corruption and delays; US public construction: design-bid-build vs design-build vs CM-at-risk, RFP/RFQ/IFB, bid tabulations, awards, contract general conditions, schedules (baseline, CPM), change orders, liquidated damages, progress payments and retention, status reports, bond oversight committees (California school construction: Prop 39 bond oversight, DSA approval, OPSC), contractor licensing and performance history sources (e.g. CSLB). What documents exist at each stage, who publishes them, what data they hold, and what typically explains a delayed or over-budget project.

A-READING.scope: Capability: reading a document with purpose. The researcher is told why the document is held (its role in the investigation), identifies what kind of document it is, studies its structure (sections, TOC, tables), reads deeper and deeper, extracts content, and develops meaning and connections, proposing facts a member accepts; a recurring kind earns an approved reading profile. Bob's words in RESUME.md.

A-PLANNING.scope: Capability: the investigation planner. From the member's words and a short interview to objectives; lines of enquiry; next steps (find document X, ask whom, records requests, settle a contradiction, test an explanation); re-planning as evidence arrives; tactical awareness of why each document and fact is held; staying on the objectives; competing explanations; when to stop; proposals a member accepts.

A-HOME.scope: Capability: the investigation's home and timeline (Bob called it a case file; in this product a 'case' is the published case, so name it without collision). One place every part of the system adds to and reads from over an investigation's life: question(s), objectives, plan, documents and why each is held, requests, explanations, findings, contradictions, waits, runs, member notes and decisions, a chronology of the subject and a log of the investigation itself. Relation to project, inquiry, intent.

A-PROCUREMENT.scope: Capability: procurement and public-contract understanding: the constructs and document kinds (RFP, bids, award, contract and its terms, schedule and milestones, change orders, payments, status reports, contractor and history) and how they map onto existing constructs (events, money, duties, progressions, entities, people, connections, standards) vs what must be added; how purpose-guided reading (READING) handles them without a hand-written reader for every variant.

A-LOOP.scope: Capability: the member in the loop. The interview at intake (clarifying questions), how proposals reach members (plan steps, facts read from documents, explanations, next acts), acceptance, correction and rejection, several members in one investigation (including disagreement, e.g. a document one member set aside that another's question needs; ruling K1618), notification doctrine (no nagging), how the member follows progress over weeks, and the answer: what the record shows, how solid, what is unknown, what action follows.

A-COST.scope: Capability: bounds, cost and trust of an autonomous investigation: run budgets, depth and breadth limits, the plan meter, cost per investigation estimated from the problem set, what runs unattended vs at a member's act (run-rules R18 and doctrine), who pays (the group's key), deployment order of run modes, evaluation (how we know the engine is good: test investigations, measures), failure modes (hallucinated facts, runaway runs, bias, privacy of people investigated).

R-3.scope: Review studies/LOOP.md and studies/COST.md, and the six studies' consistency with each other.
